REGISTER CLAIM (c) al-Tabari records ikhtilaf on WHICH night. VERIFIED against the full 6,831-char al-Tabari 44:3 block (the report itself truncates at exactly this point): 'واختلف أهل التأويل في تلك الليلة، أيّ ليلة من ليالي السنة هي؟ فقال بعضهم: هي ليلة القدر ... وقال آخرون: بل هي ليلة النصف من شعبان'. His tarjih: 'والصواب من القول في ذلك قول من قال: عنى بها ليلة القدر'. The mid-Sha'ban view is carried by 'Ikrimah (via Muhammad b. Suqah) under 44:4. The file's sentence — 'al-Tabari records some who read it as the middle night of Sha'ban — but he ... settles on Laylat al-Qadr in Ramadan' — is exactly right.

REGISTER CLAIM (d) al-Muyassar: 'إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر المباركة ... وهي في رمضان' and 'كلُّ أمر محكم من الآجال والأرزاق في تلك السنة'. Both the annual-decree reading (في تلك السنة) and the Laylat al-Qadr identification VERIFIED verbatim. Corroborated by al-Jalalayn 44:4 ('التي تكون في السنة إلى مثل تلك الليلة') and Ibn Kathir.
mubin (44:2) = ADJ|ACT|PCPL|(IV)|ROOT:byn. Form IV active participle VERIFIED by corpus; al-Jalalayn independently glosses it actively, 'المُظْهِر الحَلال مِن الحَرام'.

ADAB CHECK PASSED. The file does NOT settle 44:3 silently. It flags the question mid-body ('Which night this is, the early scholars did debate — hold the question') and reports the ikhtilaf explicitly in the closing, naming the dissenting position (middle night of Sha'ban), attributing it to al-Tabari's record, and naming his resolution. This is the correct handling of the contested night.
claims_false: The Prophet's reply in the Ibn Sayyad account is misquoted under an Ibn Kathir attribution. File: 'Ibn Kathir records that ... *Be off with you*, the Prophet told him; *you will never exceed your measure.*' Ibn Kathir's ad-Dukhan block gives 'اخْسَأْ مَا شَاءَ اللهُ (كَانَ)' — 'Be off with you! Whatever Allah wills happens.' The phrase 'you will never exceed your measure' (اخسأ فلن تعدو قدرك) is the Bukhari/Muslim wording of the same incident, not Ibn Kathir's here. Real hadith, wrong source — a conflation of two riwayat presented as a direct quotation under a named attribution.
issues: MINOR (attribution): the 'you will never exceed your measure' wording is attributed to Ibn Kathir's ad-Dukhan block, which does not carry it. See claims_false.

MINOR (imprecision): Ibn Sayyad is described as 'a boy suspected of false prophethood'. In the canonical narrations he is the boy suspected of being the Dajjal; Ibn Kathir's block characterizes him not at all. The framing is not supported by the cited source.

MINOR (soft overreach): 'The scholars heard annual recurrence in that verb-form' attributes the annual-decree reading to the imperfect morphology of yufraqu. The sources ground annual recurrence in content and athar ('أمر السنة إلى السنة', 'في تلك السنة'), not in the verb form. The underlying claim (scholars read annual recurrence) is true; the stated basis is not theirs.

MINOR (overstated): '*Mubin* is not the adjective "clear"' is absolutist. Form IV abana is attested both transitively (to make clear) and intransitively (to be clear). The active reading is well supported here — al-Jalalayn glosses al-mubin as al-muzhir — so the file lands correctly, but the exclusion is sharper than the lexicon warrants.

MINOR (rhetoric, not error): 'he, with the majority, settles on Laylat al-Qadr' — al-Tabari grounds his tarjih in his reading of 'inna kunna mundhirin', not in a majority count. The narrations do run heavily for Laylat al-Qadr, so the characterization is fair, but it is not al-Tabari's stated reason.

PROCESS RISK (report defect, not a file error): the tafsir report exhibits the known duplicate-block defect — Ibn Kathir's identical block is reproduced under all 8 headings, and al-Muyassar's under 44:2-44:8. al-Tabari's blocks ARE correctly heading-aligned (1-6 under 44:1-6, 7-9 under 44:7-8), so no wrong-ayah attribution. But the al-Tabari block is truncated at exactly 'واختلف أهل التأويل في تلك الليلة، أيّ ...' — the ikhtilaf content the file relies on was NOT visible in the artifact in hand. The file's claim happens to be exactly correct against the full source, but it was not sourced from the report.
summary: Every countable claim in this file holds. The morphology (Form IV participle chain, passive-imperfect yufraqu, the four rabb occurrences, both Form IV causative verbs) verifies exactly against the Leeds corpus, the Arabic is canonical 8/8, and all four register claims check out against the untruncated sources — including the one the report itself truncated away. The adab check PASSES: the contested night is not settled silently; the ikhtilaf is named, the dissenting mid-Sha'ban position is stated, and al-Tabari's resolution is correctly reported. The thesis (ha-mim sealed / al-mubin clarifying; God illegible at the threshold and legible in His acts) is a homiletic reading that no source contradicts and that al-Jalalayn's active gloss of al-mubin positively supports. One real defect: the Prophet's reply in the Ibn Sayyad account is quoted in the Bukhari/Muslim wording under an 'Ibn Kathir records' frame, where Ibn Kathir's ad-Dukhan block gives a different wording. Authentic hadith, wrong source. MINOR.

claims_verified: Arabic of 44:30-33 matches canonical text exactly (canonical-verse.mjs, 4/4).

'Both words are active participles built on the causative mould' VERIFIED exactly. 'One letter apart' VERIFIED. (The 'single dot' gloss is false — see claims_false.)

muhin from the root of lowness/contempt (ROOT:hwn) VERIFIED; al-Jalalayn and al-Muyassar both gloss al-'adhab al-muhin concretely as the killing of the sons and the subjection of the women, supporting the file's 'engineered to unmake dignity' reading.

REGISTER CLAIM (c) 'ali vs the double 'ala: 44:31:5:1 EaAliyFA = N|ACT|PCPL|ROOT:Elw (Form I active participle — the file says 'an active participle again' and correctly does NOT claim Form IV). 'ala occurs exactly twice in 44:32 (44:32:3:1 and 44:32:5:1, both POS:P). Count VERIFIED.

REGISTER CLAIM (d) 'ilm and 'alamin same root: 44:32:4:1 EilomK ROOT:Elm and 44:32:6:1 Ea`lamiyna ROOT:Elm. Corpus assigns the same root to both. VERIFIED. REGISTER CLAIM (e) al-Jalalayn's 'worlds of their time' qualification IS present in the file (line 110) and the substance is correctly attributed: al-Jalalayn on 44:32 reads '﴿عَلى العالَمِينَ﴾ أيْ عالِمِي زَمانهمْ أيْ العُقَلاء'. The limiter 'of their time' (زمانهم) is genuinely his. The file also uses it correctly to bound the election: 'it named their moment, not a permanent ranking over all who would ever come.'
al-Jalalayn's gloss of 'ala 'ilm as 'from Us, of their state' VERIFIED verbatim: '﴿عَلى عِلْم﴾ مِنّا بِحالِهِمْ'.
44:29 context ('the sky did not weep for them, and neither did the earth') VERIFIED against al-Tabari's 44:29-31 block heading.
The forward pivot to the Day of Decision (yawm al-fasl, 44:40) VERIFIED as the surah's next movement.

ADAB CHECK ON 44:32 PASSED. The file installs the 'of their time' limiter, explicitly denies a permanent ranking, refuses to ethnicize ('The passage speaks to you not because you are Bani Israel but because you are inside the same structure'), notes that the three verbs are all divine so no merit is being claimed, and handles the calf as 'the shadow that must be acknowledged inside a longer story' rather than as a verdict on a people. No supersessionist or ethnic-superiority drift in either direction.
claims_false: '*Muhin. Mubin.* ... One letter apart — **a single dot of difference in the middle of the word**' (line 72). FALSE as a paleographic claim. The differing letters are ha (ه) and ba (ب), which are structurally distinct letters, not dot-variants of a shared skeleton. The dot-variant family in the rasm is ب/ت/ث/ن/ي; ه is not in it. 'One letter apart' is true; 'a single dot of difference' is not, and it is offered as visible evidence for the passage's bookend structure.

'above the worlds of their own time, says al-Jalalayn — عالَمِي زَمانهم — the peoples then alive' (line 110). The Arabic quoted is misvocalized relative to al-Jalalayn, who reads عالِمِي زَمانهمْ ('the knowing/rational ones of their time') and glosses it أيْ العُقَلاء. The vowelling عالَمِي and the rendering 'the peoples then alive' are al-Muyassar's and al-Tabari's wording (على عالَمي زمانهم / على عالمي أهل زمانهم), not al-Jalalayn's. The load-bearing limiter ('of their time') is genuinely al-Jalalayn's, so the substance holds; the quoted word and its gloss are attributed to the wrong commentator.

The passage-level reading of bala' mubin as an AFFLICTION — 'a move from one kind of difficulty to a different, and in some ways more demanding, kind'; 'Rescue did not carry them out of difficulty. It carried them from one kind of difficulty into a nobler, heavier one'; 'an affliction that examined their character' — is contradicted by the file's own sources. See issues.
issues: MODERATE — SILENTLY SETTLED IKHTILAF ON THE LOAD-BEARING WORD. The entire file hangs on bala' mubin = 'manifest trial', read as a difficulty. The sources say otherwise, and two of the three were fully visible (untruncated) in the report the author had open. (1) al-Jalalayn 44:33, printed in full in the report at line 117: '﴿ما فِيهِ بَلاء مُبِين﴾ نِعْمَة ظاهِرَة مِن فَلْق البَحْر والمَنّ والسَّلْوى وغَيْرها' — he glosses bala' mubin straight as a MANIFEST FAVOUR (ni'mah zahirah), not a trial at all. (2) al-Muyassar 44:33, also printed in full at line 113: 'ما فيه ابتلاؤهم واختبارهم؛ رخاء وشدة' — testing by ease AND hardship. (3) al-Tabari 44:33 (truncated in the report, verified against the full source) records an explicit ikhtilaf — 'واختلف أهل التأويل في ذلك البلاء' — with Qatadah saying He tried them BY HIS BLESSINGS (the rescue, the parted sea, the shading cloud, the manna and salwa) and Ibn Zayd saying by ease and hardship; al-Tabari's tarjih explicitly REFUSES to narrow it: 'وقد يكون الابتلاء والاختبار بالرخاء، ويكون بالشدّة، ولم يضع لنا دليلا ... أنه عنى بعض ذلك دون بعض'. The file reports none of this. It settles on one side of a recorded ikhtilaf without saying an ikhtilaf exists. This is the exact adab failure pattern the register was built to catch, on a file the register marked done.

MODERATE — THESIS OVERREACH. Because of the above, the thesis inverts the verse's valence. The file's title, its 'one sentence to carry', and its structural claim all assert that rescue moves you FROM one affliction INTO a heavier one: 'It is a move from one kind of difficulty to a different, and in some ways more demanding, kind' (line 141); 'a nobler, heavier one' (line 124); 'an affliction that examined their character' (line 124). The sources describe the bala' as the examination CARRIED BY the favours — the sea, the manna, the salwa — not as a second affliction. The file's own better formulation ('every sign was simultaneously a mercy and an examination paper', line 120) is close to al-Tabari and would have been defensible; the 'heavier difficulty' framing on top of it is not. The reading that the second word is an affliction is required for the muhin/mubin bookend to carry the weight the file gives it, so this is load-bearing, not decorative.
MINOR — the 'single dot of difference' claim is factually wrong (see claims_false).

MINOR — the al-Jalalayn quotation on 44:32 carries al-Muyassar's/al-Tabari's vowelling and gloss (see claims_false). The register's assertion that the divergence 'was incorporated' is TRUE in substance and slightly off in citation.

MINOR — 'Twice in one verse' (line 106) follows immediately on glossing 'ala as 'above'. Only the second 'ala in 44:32 carries the height sense; the first ('ala 'ilm) means 'on the basis of'. The count is right; the implication that the height-preposition appears twice is not.

PROCESS RISK (report defect): Ibn Kathir's block is reproduced identically under all four headings and is the running 44:17-33 narrative block; al-Tabari's blocks are correctly heading-aligned (29-31 under 44:30-31, 32-33 under 44:32-33) but truncated at '...' immediately before the bala' ikhtilaf. The al-Jalalayn and al-Muyassar divergences, however, were complete and legible in the report and were still not carried into the file.
summary: The countable layer is almost entirely sound: Form II najjayna, both muhin and mubin as Form IV active participles, 'ali as a Form I active participle, 'ala twice in 44:32, 'ilm and 'alamin on the same root — all verify exactly against the Leeds corpus, and the Arabic is canonical 4/4. The adab check on 44:32 PASSES: the al-Jalalayn 'of their time' limiter is present, the election is explicitly denied as a permanent ranking, and the file refuses both supersessionist and ethnic-superiority readings. Two countable claims fail: 'a single dot of difference' between muhin and mubin is false (ha and ba are not dot-variants), and the al-Jalalayn quotation on 44:32 carries al-Muyassar's vowelling and gloss rather than al-Jalalayn's. But the real finding is the thesis. The whole file rests on bala' mubin meaning a heavier affliction sewn inside the gift. al-Jalalayn — printed in full in the report the author had open — glosses bala' mubin as ni'mah zahirah, a manifest FAVOUR. al-Muyassar, also in full, says testing by ease AND hardship. al-Tabari records the ikhtilaf openly and then explicitly refuses to narrow it to either side. The file settles on one side without disclosing that there is a side, and then pushes past even that side into 'affliction' and 'nobler, heavier difficulty', which no source supports. Validators passed because every word was tagged correctly. The argument built on them is not sound. MODERATE.
